The dataset covers all stocks and incorporates fallback logic using 20-day average volumes to ensure reliability. By providing forward-looking volume estimates, this resource can help identify periods of heightened market activity, anticipate liquidity changes, and improve the timing and risk management of price movement predictions.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Earnings Update Emails Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset compiles analyst communications following company earnings releases, focusing on the sentiment and key financial metrics discussed in these emails. By classifying messages based on keywords such as guidance, EBIT, EBITDA, and EPS, and providing an overall sentiment score for each email, the dataset offers a unique perspective on market reactions and analyst outlooks. The information can be leveraged to gauge immediate market sentiment, anticipate price movements, and identify shifts in analyst expectations, making it a valuable resource for predicting short-term stock performance after earnings announcements.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Effect of earnings announcement model
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive view of how options markets anticipate and react to company announcements, particularly focusing on the price movement and volatility around such events. It includes detailed metrics such as implied and historical volatilities, straddle and strangle prices, open interest, option volumes, and a variety of measures quantifying both forecasted and realized price moves. By analyzing the implied price move and volatility before and after key announcements, as well as comparing these to historical outcomes, traders and analysts can better gauge market expectations, identify potential mispricings, and develop strategies to capitalize on volatility. This data is especially valuable for predicting short-term price movements and understanding the risk premium embedded in option prices around major corporate events.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: International Findings Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset offers daily snapshots of international corporate events, including earnings announcements, conference calls, dividend declarations, shareholder meetings, and other key financial events. It provides detailed metadata such as event status, timing, fiscal period, and confirmation level, along with links to press releases and filings. By tracking the timing and revisions of earnings dates, dividend actions, and other corporate events, the dataset enables researchers and traders to anticipate market-moving disclosures, identify signals of management intent, and exploit calendar-based trading strategies. Its forward-looking coverage and granular event data are valuable for predicting price movements, volatility spikes, and abnormal returns around scheduled corporate actions.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Horizon Earnings and Calendar North America
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides concise, real-time summaries of major company news events that are likely to impact market prices. Each event is tagged by topic, significance level, and includes a headline and detailed description, covering a wide range of corporate actions such as mergers, acquisitions, product launches, regulatory changes, earnings guidance, and more. The data is structured for easy integration into quantitative models, allowing users to filter by region, industry, and event type. By focusing on high-impact developments and filtering out less relevant news, this dataset enables analysts and traders to quickly identify actionable events, perform historical trend analysis, and enhance event-driven trading strategies to better predict price movements.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Deep Learning Earnings Chart Predictions
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to analyze financial time series charts, specifically focusing on earnings calendar events. By converting historical price and earnings data into images, it utilizes pre-trained convolutional neural networks to predict future stock returns over multiple horizons. The dataset includes quantile-based rankings, probability assignments, and risk-adjusted metrics, making it valuable for identifying stocks likely to outperform or underperform following earnings announcements. Its predictive signals can help traders and analysts anticipate price movements around earnings releases, enhance alpha generation, and improve portfolio decision-making by incorporating retail trader perspectives and advanced image-based modeling.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Earnings Event Risk Model
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive quantitative framework for assessing and forecasting the risk associated with upcoming corporate earnings announcements. It integrates options-implied volatility, historical price movements, and advanced statistical techniques to estimate the uncertainty and potential price impact of earnings events. The model identifies stocks with elevated earnings risk, flags potential short-selling candidates, and offers metrics for integrating earnings uncertainty into portfolio risk management. By quantifying earnings-induced volatility and comparing it to realized volatility, the dataset enables investors to anticipate outsized moves, optimize portfolio construction, and hedge against adverse earnings surprises, thereby improving risk-adjusted performance during earnings season.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Global Earnings Call Sentiment Matrix
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a structured, matrix-format aggregation of global company earnings call transcripts, focusing on sentiment and topic analytics. It leverages advanced natural language processing to extract and quantify positive, neutral, and negative sentiment probabilities from management presentations and Q&A sessions, across over 200 thematic topics. The data is filtered and enhanced with smart aggregation techniques, including rolling and daily sentiment measures, confidence scores, and relevance indicators. By capturing nuanced shifts in management tone and analyst reactions, the dataset enables researchers and investors to identify patterns and signals that may precede price movements, offering valuable insights for predictive modeling and alpha generation in equity markets.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Earnings Call Text Embedding Analytics
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides advanced quantitative features derived from the full text of US corporate earnings call transcripts. By transforming entire transcripts into high-dimensional text embeddings and applying machine learning techniques, it captures nuanced management-analyst interactions, sentiment, and narrative shifts. The dataset includes both raw and compressed embedding vectors, event-aligned metrics, and machine-generated signals such as narrative shock magnitude and projected present value. These features enable systematic analysis of qualitative information, offering predictive insights into short-term stock price movements by quantifying tone, sentiment surprises, and narrative changes that may not be immediately reflected in market prices.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Multi Aspect Earnings Call Sentiment
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides advanced, multi-aspect sentiment analysis of earnings call transcripts for thousands of public companies across the US and Europe. Using state-of-the-art natural language processing and knowledge distillation from large language models, it evaluates sentiment across key financial dimensions such as asset utilization, profitability, leverage, valuation, and cash flow. The transcripts are segmented into presentation, question, and answer sections, with chunk-wise and summary sentiment scores available for each. Binary indicators and relevance scores help filter for the most impactful segments. By quantifying positive, negative, and neutral sentiment at granular and summary levels, the dataset enables investors and researchers to detect shifts in management tone, analyst sentiment, and market outlook, providing valuable signals for predicting future price movements and earnings surprises.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: International Equity Forum Activity
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset compiles user engagement and sentiment metrics from a wide range of online forums dedicated to equity discussions across multiple countries and languages. It includes aggregated statistics such as active user counts, comment volumes, buy and sell ratings, and unique user participation for various financial instruments. By analyzing trends in forum activity and sentiment, the dataset provides valuable insights into retail investor behavior and crowd sentiment, which can serve as leading indicators for price movements. The inclusion of risk-adjusted performance metrics and benchmark correlations further enhances its utility for developing predictive models and alpha strategies based on social media-driven market signals.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: US Equity KPI Forecasts
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides forward-looking forecasts of key financial performance indicators for approximately 1,500 US-listed companies, tailored to each firm's sector and business model. Metrics commonly include revenue, gross earnings, EBITDA, and product or segment-level financials, with additional industry-specific KPIs where relevant. The forecasts are generated using an ensemble model that integrates data from over a thousand sources, including public filings and industry data. Each forecast is accompanied by measures of historical accuracy, consensus comparison, and model confidence, enabling users to assess the reliability and potential edge of the predictions. By offering granular, company-level forecasts ahead of earnings releases, this dataset is valuable for anticipating earnings surprises, sector trends, and price movements, supporting strategies such as event-driven trading, portfolio rotation, and risk management.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Text-Based Event Relationship Analysis
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset leverages advanced language models to extract and classify relationships between companies, events, and entities from unstructured text sources such as news articles, press releases, and corporate communications. By identifying the types and directions of these relationships, the dataset provides structured insights into how companies interact, form alliances, or respond to market developments. This information is valuable for predicting price movements, as changes in company relationships—such as mergers, partnerships, or competitive actions—often precede significant market reactions. The dataset enhances traditional event-driven strategies by offering a deeper, more nuanced understanding of the connections and influences within the market ecosystem.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Deep Learning Event Return Prediction
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to predict future stock returns based on event-driven financial data. By transforming time series data—such as price, volume, and event occurrences—into chart images that mimic the perspective of retail traders, the dataset enables convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract predictive features. It incorporates modules for handling earnings, news counts, and macroeconomic indicators, and provides both raw and relative return forecasts across multiple time horizons. The dataset is designed to capture the impact of corporate events, news flow, and market sentiment on asset prices, offering actionable signals for long and short trading strategies. Its multi-horizon, cross-sectional ranking and probability outputs make it a powerful tool for anticipating price movements and generating alpha in quantitative trading models.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Corporate Event Sentiment Signals
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides structured sentiment analysis and key driver metrics derived from corporate event transcripts, including earnings calls, company presentations, analyst/investor days, and guidance calls. It covers a global universe of public companies, with detailed metadata such as industry classification, identifiers, event timestamps, and document sections. The dataset quantifies sentiment at multiple granularities—overall, by section, and by key topic—using scores based on positive and negative event counts, polarity, and word counts. By capturing management and analyst tone, margin and pricing power sentiment, and deception signals, it enables investors and researchers to assess market expectations, information asymmetry, and the impact of qualitative disclosures on price movements. These insights can be used to forecast earnings surprises, volatility, and post-event price drift, supporting both discretionary and quantitative investment strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Corporate Event Driven Stock Model
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a systematic stock-selection model that leverages corporate event data and machine learning techniques to predict future stock returns. It incorporates a wide range of event types, such as earnings announcements, executive changes, product launches, and structural corporate actions, and processes them using advanced feature engineering and algorithms like elastic net and xgBoost. The model outputs normalized scores and ranks for stocks based on the predictive impact of these events, enabling users to identify potential alpha opportunities and construct long/short portfolios. By capturing both fundamental and behavioral signals from event-driven market reactions, the dataset is valuable for forecasting price movements, managing risk, and enhancing quantitative investment strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Equity Expected Move Metrics
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides quantitative estimates of the expected price movement for equities over specified time horizons, derived from options market data and volatility metrics. It includes several approaches to calculating expected moves, such as Gaussian and log-normal models, as well as straddle and strangle-based strategies. The dataset also incorporates daily option volume and liquidity filters to ensure robustness. By capturing the market's consensus on future volatility and directional risk, these metrics can be valuable for forecasting price swings, managing risk, and identifying trading opportunities ahead of major market events or earnings releases.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Regulatory Filing Sentiment Analytics
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides detailed sentiment analysis of regulatory filings, including annual, quarterly, and event-driven reports submitted by public companies. It parses filings into standardized sections and applies advanced natural language processing to quantify positive and negative sentiment, track changes over time, and summarize key sections such as risk factors and management discussion. By measuring shifts in sentiment, word counts, and thematic topics, the dataset enables investors and analysts to detect changes in corporate tone, risk disclosure, and outlook, which can be predictive of future price movements. The ability to compare historical baselines and monitor sentiment trends across filings offers valuable insights for forecasting returns, identifying market inefficiencies, and constructing alpha-generating strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Transformer Based Financial News Scores
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides daily sentiment and relevance scores for financial news articles using a custom transformer-based natural language processing model. It processes real-time news feeds, extracting and quantifying sentiment, significance, and company-level impact in a structured matrix format. By bridging the gap between raw news data and actionable signals, the dataset enables researchers and portfolio managers to efficiently identify market-moving news and assess its potential effect on asset prices. The sentiment and relevance scores can be used to enhance predictive models for price movements, support event-driven trading strategies, and diversify signal sources across companies and sectors.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Global Stock Forum Sentiment Signals
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset aggregates and enriches natural language data from major stock discussion forums across Korea, France, and Germany, focusing on retail investor conversations. By applying advanced NLP techniques, it extracts sentiment, opinion strength, and discussion volume at the stock level, providing a comprehensive view of investor mood and activity in these markets. The dataset enables quantitative analysis of crowd sentiment, which can be a leading indicator of price movements, especially in markets where retail participation is significant. By tracking shifts in sentiment and discussion intensity, users can identify potential inflection points, momentum changes, and emerging trends, making it a valuable tool for predicting short-term price action and enhancing trading strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Forward Beta Risk Prediction Model
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides forward-looking estimates of stock beta for U.S. companies, predicting their sensitivity to market movements over the next three months. The model leverages a combination of fundamental, technical, and historical data to generate more accurate beta forecasts than traditional backward-looking measures. It includes alternative risk metrics, uncertainty bands, and risk surprise probabilities, enabling investors to assess systematic risk and anticipate potential volatility shifts. By identifying stocks with changing risk profiles, the dataset supports portfolio construction, risk management, and alpha generation strategies, making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and managing exposure to market risk.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Global Institutional Fund Holdings
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides daily, account-level insights into the holdings and transactions of major institutional investors, including mutual funds, ETFs, asset managers, pension funds, and insurance companies. It features detailed tables on daily trades, holdings, and the size of the investment account panel, with metrics such as conviction holdings, boundary trades, significant transactions, and concentration measures. By tracking changes in institutional ownership, trade activity, and portfolio concentration, the dataset enables users to identify shifts in market sentiment, detect accumulation or liquidation trends, and assess the impact of large fund movements on individual securities. These insights are valuable for predicting price movements, understanding liquidity dynamics, and generating alpha through analysis of institutional behavior.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Management and Executive Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive biographical and professional information on board members and senior executives from companies worldwide. It includes details such as employment history, education, achievements, compensation, board roles, committee memberships, and network connections across organizations. By analyzing board composition, director expertise, compensation structures, and interlocking directorates, investors and researchers can assess governance quality, leadership stability, and potential strategic shifts. These insights are valuable for predicting price movements, as changes in executive leadership, board structure, or director networks often precede significant corporate actions, impact investor sentiment, and influence firm performance.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Press Release Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset contains press release information from public companies, typically published a few days before formal SEC filings such as 10-K and 10-Q reports. It includes preliminary earnings announcements, non-GAAP financial metrics, company guidance, and key operating metrics. By providing early insights into company performance and management expectations, the dataset enables investors and analysts to anticipate price movements ahead of official filings. The data is useful for identifying trends, outliers, and market sentiment, making it valuable for short-term trading strategies and event-driven analysis.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Comprehensive Fundamentals Dataset
USA:1:TOP3000.description: The dataset holds fundamental items included in a company's balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statements. Even footnote items are included for enhancements and complete coverage for some companies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Audit Analytics Directors Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive tracking of director and officer changes for US public companies, including appointments, resignations, dismissals, and other board or executive movements as disclosed in SEC filings (primarily Form 8-K Item 5.02). It includes detailed information on the individuals involved, their roles (e.g., CEO, CFO, board member), the nature and timing of the changes, and related company and auditor data. By monitoring these governance events, investors and analysts can identify potential signals of corporate strategy shifts, management instability, or governance improvements, all of which may precede significant price movements. The dataset is particularly valuable for event-driven strategies, risk assessment, and understanding the impact of leadership changes on company performance.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Direct Fundamental Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: The FactSet Fundamental dataset provides comprehensive annual and interim financial statement data, ratios, and per-share metrics for global equities, with coverage starting from 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for emerging markets. The dataset includes restated data from 2004 onward, ensuring historical accuracy and comparability. Key fields cover balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow items, as well as detailed breakdowns of assets, liabilities, equity, revenues, expenses, and key performance indicators. FactSet’s symbology enables robust cross-referencing with other datasets. This dataset is valuable for quantitative and fundamental analysis, backtesting, and model development, as it allows researchers to track company financial health, valuation, and performance over time, supporting predictive modeling of price movements based on changes in core financial metrics.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Report Footnotes
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides granular financial statement footnote data for publicly traded companies, extracted using advanced XBRL technology. It includes detailed disclosures on items such as goodwill, deferred taxes, share-based compensation, and other key financial metrics not typically found in headline financial tables. By enabling users to drill down into historical and cross-company footnote information, the dataset offers unique insights into accounting policies, risk exposures, and non-standard financial events. Such depth of information can help analysts identify hidden risks, spot trends in corporate behavior, and improve the accuracy of fundamental models for predicting price movements.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Environmental and Social Governance Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between two major financial security identifiers: RIC (Reuters Instrument Code) and Bloomberg ID. By linking these identifiers, the dataset enables seamless integration and reconciliation of securities data across platforms, supporting accurate instrument identification in multi-vendor environments. While not directly containing price or fundamental data, this mapping is essential for analysts and quantitative models that aggregate, compare, or merge datasets from different sources. Reliable cross-referencing improves data quality and enables more robust research, trading, and risk management workflows, indirectly supporting price prediction by ensuring correct instrument alignment.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Fundamental Point in Time Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides point-in-time, globally standardized fundamental financial data for over 60,000 companies, including both active and inactive firms, with daily granularity. It includes original and restated values for income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements, as well as business and geographic segment data, ratios, and company metadata. The point-in-time structure eliminates forward-looking and survivorship biases, enabling accurate historical backtesting and model development. With coverage dating back to 1989 for US companies and 1997 for non-US, this dataset is essential for constructing robust factor models, event studies, and alpha signals based on true historical financials, supporting reliable prediction of price movements and risk assessment.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Company Operating Metrics
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive, standardized financial statement data and key operating metrics for companies covering 96% of global market capitalization. It includes annual and quarterly financials, per share data, calculated ratios, pricing, and textual information, enabling deep peer comparability across industries and regions. The dataset features over 1,500 data items such as income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, segment data, and supplemental metrics, with point-in-time history, restatements, and amendments. Analysts can use this rich dataset to assess company performance, financial health, and valuation, making it highly valuable for predicting price movements, screening for investment opportunities, and building quantitative models.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Global Fundamental Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive, standardized fundamental financial data for public companies worldwide, covering over 96% of global market capitalization. It includes annual and interim/quarterly financial statements, per share data, calculated ratios, pricing, and descriptive company information. With over 1,500 data items, the dataset enables deep peer comparability and historical analysis across regions and industries. It is highly valuable for quantitative research and price prediction, as it allows for the construction of fundamental factors (such as value, quality, profitability, and growth), backtesting of investment strategies, and robust cross-sectional and time-series analysis of company performance and valuation drivers.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Fundamentals Data for US Equities
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive financial data for over 9,000 U.S. listed public companies, sourced directly from their annual (10-K) and quarterly (10-Q) SEC filings. It includes a wide array of key financial metrics such as revenue, net income, assets, and operating income, all error-checked and normalized for consistency. The data is updated rapidly after new filings, ensuring timely access to the latest financial information. Analysts and investors can leverage this dataset to perform in-depth financial analysis, build quantitative models, and identify trends or anomalies that may signal future price movements, making it a valuable resource for equity research and predictive analytics.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Additional Factor Model
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RIC) for securities. It serves as a cross-reference tool, enabling users to link and reconcile data across platforms that use different security identifiers. While it does not contain price or fundamental data itself, it is essential for integrating datasets from multiple sources, ensuring consistency in security identification, and facilitating more accurate analysis and modeling. This mapping is particularly useful for researchers and portfolio managers who need to merge or compare datasets, track securities across systems, and support robust data management workflows in multi-vendor environments.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Energy Fundamental Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive asset-level, financial, regulatory, and operational data for thousands of electric utilities, natural gas companies, and coal, nuclear, and renewables plants across North America. It includes detailed information on proposed projects, streaming power price and demand data from all major Independent System Operators, and commodity price points for spot, forwards, and futures markets. The dataset also covers rate cases, regulatory events, company identification, and financial metrics such as return on equity, rate base, and capital structure. By integrating market prices, operational performance, regulatory outcomes, and company fundamentals, this resource enables analysts to assess utility and energy company health, forecast price movements, and evaluate the impact of regulatory changes and market dynamics on asset values and stock performance.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Company Fundamental Data for Equity
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive, point-in-time global company fundamental data, capturing daily snapshots of financial statements, balance sheets, cash flows, and key ratios as they were known to the market at each historical date. It includes restatements, amendments, and all changes, ensuring accurate backtesting and minimizing look-ahead bias. The dataset covers a wide range of standardized and normalized financial metrics across regions and industries, making it a critical resource for quantitative research, factor modeling, and alpha generation. By reflecting the true information set available to investors at any given time, it enables robust prediction of price movements and supports the development of systematic investment strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Factor Ratios and its Rank Model
USA:1:TOP3000.description: Raw Fundamental Ratios and Rank Data. A global time series of the raw data that is used to compute stock factors and the ranks of the factors. Raw ratios are the underlying factor ratios that are calculated using specific methodologies. To compute ranks, we sort the raw ratios in ascending/descending order based on the factor and then rank them from 1 – 100. 1 being the best and 100 the least preferable. The start date for US and US5000 files is 01/01/2009, the start date for non-US files is 01/01/2013.

It is essential for data integration, linking, and harmonization in multi-vendor environments, supporting accurate security identification for trading, portfolio management, and research workflows. While not directly predictive of price movements, it facilitates the aggregation and analysis of market and fundamental data from different sources, thereby improving the reliability and completeness of quantitative models and backtesting.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Comprehensive Fundamental Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs) and Bloomberg IDs for global securities. It enables users to cross-reference and link securities across two major financial data platforms, facilitating seamless integration of datasets from different sources. The mapping covers a wide range of asset classes and regions, supporting data normalization and consolidation for research, analytics, and operational workflows. By ensuring accurate identifier matching, this dataset is essential for portfolio management, risk analysis, and multi-source data aggregation, ultimately improving the reliability of price movement predictions and historical backtesting.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Fundamental Indicators
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive aggregate fundamental indicators for a wide range of U.S. stock market industries and sectors. It includes metrics such as gross margin, operating margin, asset turnover, current ratio, debt-to-equity, capital expenditures to sales, free cash flow to sales, sales to enterprise value, EBITDA to enterprise value, book-to-market value, earnings yield, tax rate, return on equity, return on capital, and various dividend-related ratios. The data is organized by industry, sector, and sub-industry using the Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS), and is available as market capitalization-weighted averages, percentiles, and medians. By tracking these aggregated financial health indicators over time, investors and analysts can identify industry trends, assess sector strength or weakness, and generate signals that may help predict future price movements or inform sector rotation strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Stock Reports Plus
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs and Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs), facilitating the cross-referencing of securities across different financial data platforms. By enabling seamless integration of data from multiple sources, it helps analysts and quantitative researchers ensure accurate security identification and aggregation of information. While not directly predictive of price movements, this mapping is essential for constructing robust multi-source datasets, which can improve the reliability of signals and models used in price prediction and risk analysis.

researchPapers.title: Research Paper: Using Abnormal Analyst Coverage to Unlock New Evidence on Stock Price Crash Risk

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Global Seasonal Regime Return Signals
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides predictive return signals for global equities by modeling the impact of calendar seasonality, corporate event timing, market regime context, and key data sources such as price-volume, analyst forecasts, options, and fundamentals. Each module isolates a specific data aspect—like price-volume trends, analyst revisions, or option-implied signals—and overlays contextual features such as month/quarter effects, proximity to earnings or guidance events, and prevailing market regimes (e.g., risk-on/off, expansion/contraction). The dataset is strictly point-in-time and D1-lagged to avoid lookahead bias, making it robust for research and production use. By enabling detailed analysis of how individual features and market contexts drive return predictions, it supports advanced quantitative modeling, event studies, and adaptive strategies across diverse market conditions.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Global Corporate Hiring Trends
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset tracks job opening activity for over 3,300 publicly listed companies worldwide, focusing on those with a market capitalization above $1 billion. It provides daily and historical counts of new and total job openings, along with full-text job descriptions, job types, and geographic details. The data is structured to allow analysis by sector, industry, and company, including subsidiaries and technology trends mentioned in job postings. By monitoring changes in hiring activity, investors can gain early insights into corporate growth, expansion, or contraction, which often precede shifts in revenue, operational momentum, and ultimately, stock price movements. This makes the dataset valuable for forecasting company performance and identifying macroeconomic or sector-specific trends.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Oil Price Resilience Scores
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID), facilitating seamless integration and cross-referencing of securities across two major financial data platforms. By enabling accurate identification and linkage of securities, the dataset supports portfolio managers, analysts, and researchers in consolidating data from multiple sources, improving data quality, and reducing operational risk. While not directly predictive of price movements, it is essential for ensuring data integrity in multi-source quantitative models and for efficient trade execution and compliance reporting.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Smart Insider Transaction Aggregates
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a structured, matrix-format view of insider trading activity, where individual transactions by company insiders are aggregated and filtered using advanced methodologies. By summarizing key metrics such as average shares bought or sold, and applying smart filters to highlight the most relevant transactions, the dataset enables researchers and investors to efficiently identify patterns of insider behavior across companies and regions. Such aggregated insider activity is a valuable signal for predicting future price movements, as it can reveal informed trading ahead of significant corporate events or shifts in company fundamentals. The matrix structure makes it easier to incorporate these insights into quantitative models and backtesting frameworks, supporting the development of alpha-generating investment strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Global Insider Transaction Features
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive, structured features derived from global insider transactions, including purchases, sales, awards, and option exercises by company executives, directors, and major shareholders. It covers multiple regions and asset classes, with detailed metadata such as transaction type, insider role, ownership connection, trade significance, and post-transaction holdings. By aggregating and analyzing these transactions, the dataset enables the identification of potentially informative trades, such as opportunistic buying or selling, which can signal future price movements due to information asymmetry. Quantitative models and event studies built on this data can help forecast abnormal returns, enhance alpha generation, and improve risk-adjusted portfolio performance by leveraging the predictive power of insider activity.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Aggregated Insider Transaction Matrix
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a structured matrix of insider transaction data, organized by company, region, and time delay. It aggregates and filters insider buying and selling activities, capturing key metrics such as average buy and sell values, transaction counts, and ratios over configurable time windows. By summarizing insider trades from individuals with privileged access to non-public information, the dataset enables analysts to identify patterns of opportunistic or routine trading, cluster buying, and other signals that may precede significant price movements. The smart aggregation and filtering enhance signal quality, making it a valuable resource for predicting future stock performance, detecting market anomalies, and constructing alpha-generating investment strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Global Insider Transaction Aggregates
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a structured matrix of aggregated insider transaction data across global markets, utilizing advanced filtering and smart aggregation techniques. It captures detailed information on insider trades, including buy and sell activity, transaction types, insider roles, and trade significance, organized by region and time delay. By consolidating and summarizing insider trading patterns, the dataset enables researchers and investors to identify potential signals of future price movements, such as cluster buying or selling by key executives. The aggregation and enhancement of raw insider data into a matrix format make it easier to analyze trends, detect anomalies, and generate predictive signals for alpha generation, supporting both event-driven and quantitative investment strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Global Insider Trading Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID), serving as a cross-reference for security identifiers across two major financial data platforms. It is essential for researchers, portfolio managers, and quantitative analysts who need to integrate or reconcile data from both Refinitiv and Bloomberg sources. By enabling accurate and efficient linkage of securities across systems, this mapping facilitates robust multi-source data analysis, backtesting, and model development, ultimately supporting more reliable and timely investment decision-making and price prediction workflows.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: SEC Report Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive, standardized fundamental financial data for global companies, including annual and quarterly balance sheets, income statements, cash flow statements, and key financial ratios. It covers a wide range of metrics such as revenues, earnings, assets, liabilities, equity, and cash flows, as well as detailed industry classifications (GICS, SIC, NAICS), company identifiers (GVKEY, CUSIP, ISIN, SEDOL, ticker), and corporate actions. The data is point-in-time, capturing both original and restated values, and is structured to support robust historical analysis and backtesting. By offering granular, high-quality financials and corporate event data, this dataset enables researchers and investors to build and test predictive models, assess company health, and identify drivers of price movements across global equity markets.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Ownership Model Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive global coverage of equity ownership by institutions, mutual funds, and insiders/stakeholders, with detailed position-level data for each security and holder. It includes both summary and granular holdings, sourced from regulatory filings such as SEC 13F, UK Share Register, and other international disclosures. The data tracks current and historical positions, market values, portfolio characteristics, and investment styles, enabling analysis of ownership trends, concentration, and changes over time. By revealing shifts in institutional and insider holdings, the dataset helps identify informed trading, herding, and market sentiment, which are critical for predicting price movements, liquidity changes, and potential catalysts in global equities.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Short Sale Volume Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides detailed information on short sale trading activity for U.S. equities, including metrics such as short volume, short exempt volume, total trade volume, and trade-level details like symbol, date, time, size, and price. The data is sourced from multiple trade reporting facilities and covers regular trading hours, offering a comprehensive view of short selling across major U.S. exchanges and off-exchange venues. By analyzing trends in short sale volume relative to total volume, market participants can gauge bearish sentiment, identify potential short squeezes, and anticipate price movements driven by short covering or increased short interest. This dataset is valuable for traders, analysts, and quantitative researchers seeking to enhance predictive models and risk management strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Institutions and Beneficial Stake Ownership
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive information on global equity ownership by institutions, mutual funds, and beneficial stakeholders. It includes current and historical holdings data from over 50,000 portfolios and companies across 70 countries, with more than 10 years of history. Key fields cover shares held, percent of shares outstanding, report dates, aggregated statistics, and investor profiles. The dataset enables analysis of institutional buying and selling activity, ownership concentration, and changes in major holders, which are critical for understanding market sentiment, liquidity, and potential price movements. By tracking shifts in institutional positions and identifying new or reduced stakes, investors and researchers can anticipate trends, detect accumulation or distribution phases, and enhance predictive models for stock price behavior.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Daily Intraday Price Volume Features
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides daily aggregated features derived from intraday price and volume data across global equity markets. By processing interval-level trading statistics—such as bid-ask spreads, order book depth, trade counts, volatility, and volume—into daily summaries, it enables consistent cross-regional analysis despite differences in exchange hours and data structures. These features are valuable for quantitative researchers and portfolio managers seeking to generate alpha signals, as they capture nuanced intraday market dynamics that can precede price movements. The dataset’s unified format and broad coverage make it a powerful tool for predicting short-term price changes and enhancing trading strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Index Reconstitution Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive information on global index reconstitution events, including the addition and deletion of stocks or companies from various equity indexes, their respective weight percentages, and detailed hedge ratio data. It covers dynamic and static hedge ratios for both indexes and currencies, as well as currency pair exposures and effective dates. The dataset also includes metrics such as momentum and interest rates, along with position weights and returns for index components. By tracking changes in index composition, weights, and hedging strategies, this dataset enables analysts to identify shifts in market sentiment, sector rotation, and currency risk management, which are critical for forecasting price movements and understanding the impact of index rebalancing on asset prices.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Multi Factor Model Universal Output
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides the output of proprietary multi-factor risk models in a standardized format compatible with widely used risk models such as Barra and Uber. It enables portfolio managers and researchers to access daily, point-in-time factor exposures, risk estimates, and groupings for US equities, facilitating integration with simulation and portfolio construction tools. The dataset leverages advanced machine learning clustering techniques on company fundamentals and price data to create robust, dynamically updated groupings that capture stock co-movement and risk structure beyond static sector classifications. By offering comprehensive, daily-updated risk model outputs, this dataset supports more accurate risk control, portfolio optimization, and alpha signal neutralization, ultimately helping users better predict and manage price movements and portfolio risk.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Machine Learning Factor Projections
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides machine learning-generated projection features for US equities, leveraging advanced neural network architectures such as multi-layer perceptrons, self-attention mechanisms, and convolutional neural networks. It synthesizes a wide array of quantitative factor models—including value, growth, momentum, quality, liquidity, and management quality—by integrating both traditional financial metrics and alternative data sources. The resulting features are designed to capture complex, non-linear relationships in the data, offering enhanced predictive signals for future price movements. By combining insights from multiple factor themes and updating models with new data, this dataset can help investors identify stocks with favorable risk-return profiles and anticipate shifts in market trends, making it a valuable tool for systematic portfolio construction and alpha generation.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Multilingual NLP News Sentiment Signals
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides enriched sentiment signals for financial news by leveraging a scalable, multilingual natural language processing (NLP) framework. Initially built on top of Benzinga news and designed to expand to other text-based sources, it distills insights from large language models into efficient, production-ready NLP pipelines. The dataset includes fields such as average character count, AFINN and Loughran-McDonald sentiment scores, and supports coverage for the top 3000 US stocks. By offering standardized, high-frequency sentiment metrics across multiple languages and news sources, this dataset enables quantitative researchers and traders to systematically capture shifts in market sentiment, identify news-driven trading opportunities, and enhance predictive models for price movements.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Research Indicators
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive short interest and technical indicator data for US equities, ADRs, and ETFs. It includes measures such as short interest ratio, short intensity rank, days to cover, and classifications of shorting activity (heavy, moderate, light). Additionally, it features proprietary technical ranks, power ranks, sector and group rankings, and various moving average and trend indicators. The dataset also covers option sentiment metrics, seasonality patterns, and momentum indicators. By combining short interest data with technical and sentiment analysis, the dataset enables users to identify potential short squeezes, long squeezes, and contrarian trading opportunities. This multifaceted approach helps predict price movements by highlighting stocks with unusual short activity, strong or weak technicals, and shifts in market sentiment, making it valuable for both quantitative and discretionary trading strategies.

The data includes both historical and forward-looking measures, as well as revisions and surprises, enabling robust multifactor modeling and risk analysis. By integrating fundamental, technical, and sentiment factors, the dataset supports the development and backtesting of predictive models for stock selection, portfolio construction, and risk management, making it highly valuable for forecasting price movements and identifying alpha opportunities across global markets.

The dataset includes sector-neutralized scores and composite innovation signals, which are used in advanced alpha models to identify stocks with strong technological momentum and relevance. By analyzing the evolution and impact of a firm's technology base, the dataset helps investors predict price movements by highlighting companies likely to outperform due to superior innovation, while also supporting market-neutral and pairs trading strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Risk Parity Method Model
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive quantitative model for value investing, utilizing dynamic regime switching, risk mitigation techniques, and multifactor analysis. It includes composite scores based on price-to-earnings, dividend yield, free cash flow yield, operating cash flow yield, and book-to-market ratios, all adjusted for sector, exposure, and correlation biases. The model outputs daily and monthly updated scores for the top 3000 US stocks, supporting both market neutral and long-only strategies. By combining adaptive factor exposures and risk parity methods, the dataset helps identify undervalued securities while minimizing downside risk, making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and constructing robust investment portfolios.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: ETF Based Equity Factors

It includes detailed metrics on ETF inflows, outflows, net flows, trading intensity, popularity, and changes in ETF holdings at the individual stock level. By aggregating ETF creation and redemption flows, as well as tracking the percentage of shares held by ETFs, the dataset enables users to identify trends in institutional demand, liquidity shifts, and crowding effects. These factors are highly relevant for building multi-factor and cross-sectional risk models, and can be used to predict short-term price movements, mean-reversion opportunities, and potential volatility in US equities.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Stock Selection from Accounting-based Factors
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset contains a comprehensive suite of Performance Deviation Index (PDI) factors derived from 14 key accounting variables, designed to measure the deviation of a company's latest financial metrics from its historical averages. The dataset includes composite models, quality-focused variants, and sector-neutralized signals, all constructed using advanced techniques such as risk parity weighting, deseasonalization, and clustering. By capturing anomalies and behavioral biases in financial statement data, these factors have demonstrated superior risk-adjusted returns compared to traditional accounting ratios and growth metrics. The dataset is valuable for quantitative investors seeking to enhance stock selection, improve portfolio diversification, and boost predictive power for price movements across global equity markets.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Sensitivity to the Inflation Change
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides stock-level sensitivity estimates to expected inflation, using changes in breakeven rates and advanced machine learning techniques such as elastic net regression. It covers a wide range of global equities and includes sector, country, and performance metrics, allowing users to analyze how individual stocks and sectors respond to inflationary pressures. By quantifying inflation beta and related exposures, the dataset is valuable for portfolio managers and analysts seeking to forecast price movements, manage risk, and implement tactical asset allocation strategies in environments with changing inflation expectations.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Stock Selection DL model

It includes both raw and processed model scores, updated daily and with monthly historical data, covering a broad universe of equities across multiple regions. The model leverages advanced neural network architectures such as CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, transformers, and conformers, and is engineered to be interpretable and relatively uncorrelated with common equity style factors. The dataset is particularly valuable for systematic and high-frequency trading strategies, as it offers timely, actionable signals that can be used to enhance portfolio construction, manage risk, and exploit short-term price inefficiencies. The dataset is designed to eliminate forward-looking and survivorship biases, enabling accurate backtesting and robust quantitative research. By offering point-in-time snapshots of income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements, along with detailed metadata on restatements, reporting currency, and auditor opinions, it allows researchers and investors to model and predict price movements based on true historical financial information, supporting factor research, event studies, and systematic investment strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides market-implied values for quantitative alpha model signals by applying advanced deep learning techniques to vendor-supplied alpha model data, specifically from the QSG factor library. By leveraging price and volume data, the model estimates what the market "implies" about the value of each alpha factor, rather than relying solely on raw or fundamental inputs. The methodology includes dynamic clustering, time-series feature engineering, and dimension reduction to generate robust, uncorrelated groupings and predictions. The resulting market-implied factor values can be used to identify discrepancies between model signals and market expectations, offering a unique perspective for forecasting price movements, detecting potential mispricings, and enhancing alpha generation in systematic trading strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Time-series prediction of alpha models
USA:1:TOP3000.description: The Starmine dataset provides two key quantitative models: the Earnings Quality (EQ) model and the Analyst Revisions Model (ARM). The EQ model ranks global stocks (percentile 1-100) based on the sustainability and reliability of reported earnings, using a multi-factor approach that incorporates accruals, cash flow, operating efficiency, and exclusions (such as the difference between pro forma and GAAP earnings). The ARM model also ranks stocks (percentile 1-100) by tracking changes in analyst sentiment, including revisions to earnings estimates, revenue forecasts, and recommendations. Both models are sector- and region-neutral, and are designed to predict future analyst revisions and price movements. The dataset includes detailed subcomponent scores, flags for data quality, and is available globally with daily updates. These models are widely used for stock selection, risk management, and alpha generation, as they have demonstrated strong predictive power for future returns and can be used to identify stocks with improving fundamentals or deteriorating earnings quality.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Research Analyst Estimate Factors

It also includes measures of analyst coverage and dispersion in earnings estimates, offering insight into market attention and consensus. By tracking changes in analyst sentiment, forecast revisions, and recommendation trends, the dataset helps identify shifts in market expectations and potential catalysts for price movement. Investors and researchers can use these factors to anticipate earnings-related volatility, detect sentiment-driven momentum, and enhance predictive models for stock returns.

USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides detailed open-close trade profiles for options traded on the C1, C2, BZX, and EDGX exchanges. It aggregates and categorizes option trading volume by participant type (customer, professional customer, broker-dealer, market maker), trade direction (buy/sell), and position status (opening/closing), with further breakdowns by trade size. The data includes key option contract details such as underlying symbol, strike, expiry, type (call/put), and open interest, as well as price statistics. By analyzing the flow of opening and closing trades across different participant types and trade sizes, researchers can infer market sentiment, detect unusual activity, and build predictive signals for price movements in the underlying securities. This granularity is especially valuable for understanding the behavior of different market participants and for constructing order flow-based alphas.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Equity Options Moneyness Aggregates
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides intermediate, derived metrics on implied volatility and pricing for US equity options, sourced from comprehensive historical options data. It includes key option sensitivities (Greeks), interpolated volatility surfaces, and standardized pricing information, enabling detailed analysis of market expectations and risk sentiment. By capturing nuanced changes in implied volatility and option pricing, the dataset is valuable for forecasting short-term price movements, identifying volatility risk premia, and constructing systematic trading strategies based on options market signals. Its granularity and breadth make it a powerful tool for quantitative research and predictive modeling in equity markets.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Implied Volatility and Pricing for Equity Options
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive historical data on implied volatility, pricing, and sensitivities for European listed equity and index options. It includes detailed information on option contracts such as strike price, expiration date, open interest, volume, bid/ask prices, and option Greeks (delta, gamma, vega, theta). The dataset also covers underlying security prices, dividend conventions, and interest rate curves used for option pricing. With interpolated volatility surfaces and standardized option metrics, it enables robust analysis of market sentiment, risk, and volatility dynamics. Researchers and traders can leverage this data to forecast price movements, identify arbitrage opportunities, and develop systematic trading strategies based on volatility and option market activity across European markets.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Options Analytics Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides daily historical and option-implied volatility metrics for over 2,500 US equities, including close-to-close and Parkinson historical volatilities across multiple time horizons, as well as at-the-money implied volatilities for calls, puts, and their averages. It also features skew steepness indicators, offering insight into the volatility term structure and skew for each stock. By combining realized and market-implied volatility measures, the dataset enables quantitative analysts and traders to assess market expectations, identify volatility risk premiums, and detect shifts in sentiment or risk, which are valuable for forecasting price movements, constructing volatility-based strategies, and managing portfolio risk.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Forecasted Volatility for Equity Options
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive forecasts of option volatility metrics for all US-listed stocks, ETFs, and equity indices. It includes predictions for the next 20 days of historical and implied volatility, long-term at-the-money implied volatility, and detailed measures of volatility skew and curvature across strikes. The data also covers relationships with major benchmarks like SPY and related ETFs, offering insights into market-wide and asset-specific volatility dynamics. By analyzing these forward-looking volatility estimates and their term structures, traders and quantitative analysts can better anticipate price movements, identify potential risk events, and construct more effective options strategies for hedging, speculation, or volatility arbitrage.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Volatility Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive daily volatility metrics for over 2,500 US equities, including both historical and option-implied volatilities across multiple time horizons. It features close-to-close and Parkinson historical volatility calculations, as well as at-the-money implied volatilities for calls, puts, and their averages, spanning durations from 10 to 1080 calendar days. Additionally, it includes skew steepness indicators to capture volatility asymmetries. By analyzing the interplay between historical and implied volatility, as well as volatility skew, traders and quantitative analysts can better anticipate price movements, identify periods of heightened risk, and develop options-based trading strategies that exploit volatility mispricings or forecast market direction.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Options Analytics
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive option-driven metrics for over 2,500 US equities, updated daily using end-of-day market data. It includes put/call ratios based on both trading volume and open interest across multiple future time horizons, forward prices, and breakeven levels for all, call, and put options. These metrics are calculated for constant terms ranging from 10 to 1,080 calendar days, offering granular insights into market sentiment, positioning, and expected price levels. By analyzing shifts in put/call ratios, forward prices, and breakeven points, traders and analysts can gauge investor sentiment, identify potential price inflection points, and enhance predictive models for equity price movements.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Option Chart Image Return Prediction
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset consists of 2D financial chart images generated from historical option market data, including implied volatility curves and OHLC price charts, for individual stocks. Using these images, a convolutional neural network (CNN) model is trained to predict future single-stock returns, both as raw values and as quantile rankings relative to peers. The dataset provides model outputs such as predicted returns, quantile labels, and associated confidence probabilities for multiple forecast horizons. By leveraging visual patterns in option data, the dataset enables systematic, cross-sectional return predictions and can help identify stocks with favorable risk-reward profiles, making it a valuable tool for quantitative trading and investment strategies focused on price movement forecasting.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: US Equity Option Horizon Decomposition
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive decomposition of US equity option and volatility analytics into short, medium, and long time horizons. By applying advanced filtering and decomposition techniques to the original option ratings, analytics, volatility, and risk metrics, it generates horizon-specific fields for each underlying metric, such as implied volatility ratings, put-call ratios, liquidity ratings, historical volatility, and risk measures. This multi-horizon approach enables researchers and traders to isolate and analyze alpha signals and risk exposures that are specific to different investment timeframes. The dataset is particularly valuable for horizon-focused alpha research, allowing users to identify independent and low-correlation trading signals, optimize portfolio turnover, and enhance predictive models for price movements by leveraging the distinct behaviors of option and volatility metrics across various time horizons.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Options Derived Composite Signals
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a multifactor composite model score for stock selection, derived from over 80 options-based signals. It aggregates features such as implied volatility, option Greeks, liquidity measures, and sentiment indicators, offering a quantitative view of market dynamics from the options market. By integrating these options-derived factors with traditional equity signals like value, momentum, and quality, the dataset enables investors to enhance their predictive models and systematic strategies. The composite score can be used directly for screening or as a benchmark, helping analysts and portfolio managers identify stocks with favorable risk-return profiles and anticipate price movements based on options market activity.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Order Book Liquidity and Imbalance Analytics
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset offers comprehensive analytics derived from Level 1 to Level 3 order books for US and EU equities, focusing on liquidity, order flow, and trade imbalances. It includes metrics such as auction dislocation, order imbalance, liquidity around best bid and offer, trade aggressiveness, and spread measurements. The data also covers order placement, modification, execution behaviors, and venue price quality, providing insights into market microstructure and trading dynamics. By analyzing these metrics, users can identify periods of liquidity stress, anticipate price movements driven by order imbalances, and assess the impact of aggressive trading activity. This information is valuable for predicting short-term price changes, optimizing execution strategies, and understanding the drivers of volatility in equity markets.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Institutional Order Flow Imbalance
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive view of order flow imbalances across various market participant classes, including firms, brokers, dealers, market makers, customers, and professional customers. It quantifies the net difference between bullish and bearish option trading activity for each group, using normalized metrics based on the volume and number of trades. By distinguishing between buy and sell actions in call and put contracts, the dataset reveals shifts in sentiment and positioning among different investor types. Such granular imbalance data is highly valuable for predicting short-term price movements, as persistent order flow imbalances often precede changes in underlying asset prices. Analysts and traders can leverage these insights to identify potential reversals, momentum shifts, and periods of heightened market activity, thereby enhancing the accuracy of trading strategies and risk management models.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Global Executive Performance Factors
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg Global Identifiers (BBGID) and Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC), two widely used security identifiers in financial markets. By linking these identifiers, the dataset enables seamless cross-referencing of securities across Bloomberg and Refinitiv platforms, facilitating data integration, portfolio management, and research workflows. While not directly predictive of price movements, accurate identifier mapping is essential for consolidating data from multiple sources, ensuring data integrity, and supporting robust quantitative analysis and trading strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Transaction Volume Data for Equity
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive, anonymized daily trading activity for U.S. equities, capturing all volume cleared through the National Securities Clearing Corporation. It breaks down trading by security and transaction type—buy, sell, short sell, and short sell exempt—across the entire market and key broker peer groups. Key metrics include total volume, volume-weighted average price (VWAP), broker participation counts, and market concentration measures. By analyzing imbalances between buy and sell activity, short selling trends, and shifts in broker market share, users can identify liquidity changes, detect unusual trading patterns, and anticipate potential price movements. The dataset is particularly valuable for quantitative analysts and portfolio managers seeking to enhance trading strategies, monitor market structure, and generate predictive signals based on real-time shifts in supply and demand dynamics.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: details data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBID) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RIC), facilitating the cross-referencing of securities across two major financial data platforms. By enabling seamless integration and reconciliation of security identifiers, it supports accurate data aggregation, portfolio management, and multi-source analytics. While not directly predictive of price movements, this mapping is essential for researchers and analysts who need to merge datasets, track instruments across systems, and ensure consistency in security-level analysis, which can indirectly enhance the quality and reliability of quantitative models and trading strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Corporate Earnings Call Sentiment Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg IDs, enabling users to cross-reference securities across two major financial data platforms. The mapping is essential for integrating, reconciling, and aggregating data from Bloomberg and Refinitiv sources, facilitating seamless data analysis and portfolio management. While not directly predictive of price movements, the dataset is crucial for ensuring data consistency and accuracy in multi-source financial research, allowing analysts and quants to link disparate datasets and enhance the reliability of their models and analytics.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Equity Swap Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBIDs), facilitating cross-platform security identification. By enabling seamless translation between two major financial data vendor codes, it supports data integration, reconciliation, and aggregation across trading, risk, and research systems. While not directly predictive of price movements, accurate identifier mapping is essential for merging datasets, tracking instruments across sources, and ensuring consistency in multi-vendor analytics, which indirectly enhances the reliability of price prediction models and market analysis.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Sensitivity to Interest Rates Model
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a machine learning-based model that quantifies the sensitivity of individual stocks to changes in interest rates, using elastic net regression. It includes metrics such as sensitivity to parallel shifts (level) and twists (slope) of the yield curve, derived from principal component analysis of global interest rate data. Covering over 11,000 stocks across 45 countries, the dataset enables investors to assess how monetary policy changes and yield curve movements may impact stock returns. By incorporating these sensitivity measures into portfolio construction and risk management, users can better predict price movements during periods of interest rate volatility and optimize exposure to macroeconomic factors.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Multi-Region Dividend Alpha Model Dataset
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset contains the outputs and components of a machine learning-based global stock selection model focused on dividend-paying equities. Leveraging a large factor library and advanced algorithms, it generates composite scores that reflect the expected performance and risk profile of stocks, with specialized sub-models for linear, hedge, and defensive scenarios. The model incorporates contextual information, risk management, and signal persistence metrics, making it highly effective for constructing portfolios that seek stable income and downside protection. By providing predictive signals and risk-adjusted rankings, this dataset is valuable for forecasting price movements, optimizing portfolio returns, and managing risk in dividend-oriented investment strategies.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Web Comments & Reaction Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset captures user-generated comments, replies, and reactions (likes/dislikes) from the community pages of Russell 3000 Index stocks. It provides granular insights into investor sentiment, discussion trends, and reaction intensity for individual companies and events. By analyzing the volume, tone, and engagement of social conversations, researchers can gauge market sentiment shifts, identify emerging narratives, and potentially forecast short-term price movements driven by retail investor activity and crowd psychology. The dataset is especially valuable for sentiment analysis, event-driven trading strategies, and monitoring real-time market mood.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: NLP on conference conversation
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset applies natural language processing to corporate event transcripts, primarily from earnings calls and other financial conferences, to extract and quantify sentiment. It includes detailed breakdowns by section (presentation, Q&A), speaker, and sentence, providing sentiment scores using dictionary-based matching. The data is cleaned and segmented for ease of use, with meta data and simple sentiment indicators for each event. By analyzing the tone and sentiment of management and analyst interactions, investors can gauge market expectations, management confidence, and potential red flags, making this dataset valuable for predicting short-term price movements and identifying alpha opportunities around key corporate events.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Dividend model
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset identifies and predicts companies most likely to reduce, suspend, or terminate their dividend payments, focusing on so-called "dividend laggards." Leveraging a global factor library and machine learning algorithms, the model analyzes historical and real-time data to flag firms at risk of dividend cuts, which often precede significant share price declines and continued underperformance. By providing early warning signals on potential dividend reductions, the dataset is valuable for investors seeking to avoid downside risk, implement short strategies, or optimize portfolio yield, especially during periods of economic stress when dividend suspensions become more prevalent.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Relationship enhanced with AI/ML
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RICs) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBIDs), enabling seamless cross-referencing of securities across two major financial data platforms. This mapping is essential for portfolio managers, analysts, and data engineers who need to reconcile, aggregate, or compare security-level information across systems. While not directly predictive of price movements, accurate identifier mapping is foundational for multi-source data analysis, backtesting, and the construction of robust trading signals and risk models.

USA:1:TOP3000.name: Linked Firms Momentum Data
USA:1:TOP3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive set of network-based momentum signals for global equities, combining traditional price momentum with advanced network analytics derived from business segments, geographic regions, analyst coverage, executive connections, innovation linkages, supply chain, and shipping data. The model leverages natural language processing on regulatory filings to identify economic linkages between companies, enhancing the predictive power and diversification of momentum strategies. By integrating multiple uncorrelated momentum factors and optimizing risk allocation, the dataset offers robust signals with higher risk-adjusted returns and lower drawdowns than conventional momentum approaches. Investors and analysts can use these insights to construct diversified portfolios and improve forecasts of future price movements.
