GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset focuses on financial opinion mining from various text-based sources such as earnings calls, news, and social media. It aims to extract potential signals by performing deep analysis, considering financial characteristics and correlations among different data sources. The methodology involves advanced feature extraction, sentiment scoring using word embeddings, semi-supervised/transfer learning for adapting sentiment across data, and time-series value prediction through multi-source embedding. The dataset is designed to cover opinion mining tasks including sentiment analysis, company grouping, and value prediction, ultimately seeking to uncover valuable insights from the complete event timeline across diverse text data.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Employee Review Data
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between two major financial security identifiers: RIC (Reuters Instrument Code) and Bloomberg ID. By linking these identifiers, the dataset enables seamless integration and cross-referencing of securities data from different financial data providers. This is particularly useful for analysts and portfolio managers who need to reconcile, aggregate, or validate security-level information across platforms. While not directly predictive of price movements, accurate identifier mapping is essential for ensuring data integrity in multi-source quantitative models, risk management systems, and trading operations.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Wikipedia Viewing Data
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset tracks daily Wikipedia pageviews for companies across a global universe, capturing user interest and information-seeking behavior. By aggregating and transforming raw pageview data into structured fields, it enables researchers to analyze trends in public attention, which can serve as a proxy for retail investor sentiment or information demand. The use of natural days (including weekends and holidays) ensures comprehensive coverage and more robust time series analysis. Spikes or sustained increases in pageviews may precede or coincide with significant price movements, making this dataset valuable for predicting market activity, especially around news events or periods of heightened public interest.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Thomson Reuters News Analytics Equities
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive news analytics for equities, including over 80 fields across five key categories: relevance, sentiment, novelty, volume, and headline classification. Each news item is scored for every asset it materially mentions, with separate linguistic processing for each asset, such as companies or commodities. The dataset includes granular metadata like timestamps, source, headline tags, and asset identifiers (RIC, PermID), enabling detailed analysis of how news impacts specific securities. By quantifying sentiment, relevance, and novelty, and tracking news volume, this dataset is highly valuable for predicting price movements, identifying market-moving events, and generating alpha signals through systematic news-based strategies.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Individual Investor Transactions Data
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset captures detailed transaction-level activity from over 81,000 individual retail users, including actions such as opening, closing, and adjusting positions, as well as watchlist modifications. It includes granular information on trade execution, portfolio types, user engagement metrics, and asset identifiers, updated frequently to reflect real-time investor behavior. By analyzing patterns in retail trading flows, sector allocations, and geographic distributions, this dataset offers valuable insights into sentiment shifts and crowd-driven market dynamics, which can be leveraged to anticipate short-term price movements and identify emerging trends in equity markets.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Predictive Analyst-Company Signal Set
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides predictive signals specifically designed for advanced analyst and company relationship modeling, leveraging deep learning on company relations and analyst estimate data. It enhances traditional analyst revision and valuation models by integrating both company-to-company (Revere) and analyst-to-company (IBES) information, resulting in higher quality and broader coverage signals, especially for global equities. The dataset includes modules that generate forward-looking signals based on changes in analyst sentiment, earnings revisions, and valuation metrics, all informed by the underlying network of business relationships. These predictive signals can be used to anticipate future price movements by capturing both direct analyst actions and the economic linkages between companies, offering a unique edge for quantitative price prediction and alpha generation.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Price Volume Data for Equity
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: The dataset contains financial data related to equities, including metrics such as prices (open, high, low, close), trading volumes, market capitalization, returns, dividends, splits, and other key indicators that provide insights into stock performance and market activity.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Microstructure Spread Data
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive spread pricing data for securities traded across the US, Canada, and Asia. It includes key fields such as the ticker symbol, the spread (difference between bid and ask prices), and spread values calculated over the last 30 minutes, both in absolute terms and in basis points. By analyzing the spread and its recent changes, traders and analysts can gauge market liquidity, trading costs, and potential price volatility. Narrowing or widening spreads can signal shifts in supply-demand dynamics, making this dataset valuable for predicting short-term price movements and identifying periods of heightened market activity.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Relationship Data for Equity
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides a mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBID) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RIC), enabling users to link securities across Bloomberg and Refinitiv platforms. The data is sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, and maintained for integration and operational purposes rather than general research. While not directly predictive of price movements, this mapping is essential for harmonizing datasets, ensuring accurate cross-platform security identification, and supporting multi-source data analysis in quantitative research and portfolio management workflows.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Holidays and Trading Hours Calendar
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: The Data Explorers dataset provides comprehensive short interest and securities lending data, sourced from the lending desks of major sell-side institutions and large buy-side players globally. It covers metrics such as lendable inventory, utilization rates, borrow demand, loan values, borrow costs, and proprietary sentiment indicators (e.g., DNS, DIPS, DIMV, DSS) at the security, group, and market level. The dataset includes both end-of-day and intraday feeds, with detailed breakdowns by region, asset class, and contributor type. By tracking the supply and demand dynamics of securities lending, as well as short positioning and borrow costs, this dataset offers valuable insights into market sentiment, short squeeze risk, and crowding. These signals are widely used in quantitative strategies to predict price reversals, identify crowded shorts, manage risk, and enhance alpha generation, making it a critical resource for anticipating price movements driven by short interest and lending market activity.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Corporate Bond Pricing Data
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of equity signals derived from corporate bond pricing data, including z-spread curves, term spreads, and principal component analysis factors such as shift, tilt, and twist. By linking bond market indicators—such as credit risk, yield curve dynamics, and bond-equity return divergences—to related equities, the dataset offers 19 base factors and several variants to predict future stock returns. These factors capture changes in credit conditions, market sentiment, and cross-asset relationships, making the dataset valuable for quantitative models, risk assessment, and alpha generation. Investors and analysts can use these signals to enhance equity selection, construct long-short strategies, and anticipate price movements based on underlying credit market trends.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Derived Industry Classification
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg IDs, two of the most widely used security identifiers in the financial industry. By linking these identifiers, the dataset enables seamless integration and cross-referencing of data from different sources, facilitating more accurate and efficient data analysis. This mapping is particularly useful for analysts and portfolio managers who work with multi-vendor data feeds, as it ensures consistency in security identification across platforms. While not directly predictive of price movements, the dataset is essential for data normalization, aggregation, and the construction of robust multi-source trading and risk models.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Alternate Industry Classification
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides an alternative industry classification for global equities, derived from historical stock returns using principal component analysis (PCA) and robust resampling methods. By extracting significant risk factors and grouping securities into clusters of varying sizes, it offers a data-driven approach to industry segmentation across multiple regions and sectors. The dataset includes detailed mappings for top securities and supports flexible cluster sizes, enabling users to analyze market structure, sector rotation, and cross-sectional risk. This classification can enhance factor modeling, portfolio construction, and alpha generation by capturing dynamic relationships between stocks, potentially improving predictions of price movements and risk exposures.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Equity Interval Data
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides standardized, point-in-time operating metrics for companies worldwide, with deep industry-specific coverage (e.g., retail, airlines, oil & gas, healthcare, REITs). Metrics include key performance indicators such as same store sales, occupancy rates, production volumes, and other operational statistics, enabling detailed peer and cross-industry comparisons. The data is updated weekly and includes both annual and quarterly frequencies, with comprehensive historical coverage. By capturing granular, comparable operational data, this dataset is valuable for quantitative research and can enhance price prediction models by linking company performance drivers to future returns, especially when combined with financial statement and market data.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Specific Return Dataset
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides daily specific returns for global equities, calculated using a proprietary risk model that extends the Barra framework with additional style and industry factors. The data includes returns orthogonal to risk model factors, representing the idiosyncratic or residual component of asset performance. Coverage spans multiple regions and universes, with fields such as Bloomberg ID and specific return percentage. By decomposing total returns into factor-driven and residual parts, this dataset enables researchers and portfolio managers to isolate stock-specific movements, assess alpha generation, and improve risk-adjusted forecasting of price changes.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Index Market Data
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides standardized, point-in-time global company fundamental data, including detailed financial statements, per share data, calculated ratios, and pricing information for over 96% of global market capitalization. It offers annual and interim/quarterly data, with 1500+ data items, and is designed for peer comparability across companies and regions. The dataset is valuable for quantitative research and price prediction, as it enables robust cross-sectional and time-series analysis of financial health, valuation, profitability, leverage, and growth metrics, which are key drivers of stock price movements and risk assessment.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: custom relationship data
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive, real-time and historical text news feed combining Dow Jones and Reuters NewsScope content. It includes headlines, full stories, alerts, and updates, all tagged with rich metadata such as company identifiers (RICs, tickers), topics, regions, and event types. The feed covers a wide range of financial, economic, corporate, and geopolitical news, with detailed classification for sectors, asset classes, and event types (e.g., earnings, M&A, regulatory actions). The dataset is structured for machine readability and includes both breaking news and in-depth analysis, making it highly suitable for quantitative research, event-driven trading, and sentiment analysis. By providing timely and granular news data, it enables the detection of market-moving events, sentiment shifts, and thematic trends, which can be leveraged to predict price movements and inform trading strategies.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Corporate Action Dataset
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset looks at corporate events that can affect stock prices, such as delisting, merger, stock splits, etc. One can analyze the effect of corporate actions on stock prices and develop alphas based on event-driven opportunities.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Intraday Tick Data and Statistics
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides market-implied values for key fundamental financial metrics, such as earnings, cash flow, debt, and profitability, derived from quantitative models that invert the typical relationship between fundamentals and price. By estimating what the market expects a company’s next quarter fundamentals to be—based on current price data and historical alpha signals—it offers a forward-looking proxy for anticipated earnings releases and financial health. The dataset includes prediction errors and volatility measures, enabling users to assess the accuracy and dispersion of market expectations. This information is valuable for forecasting price movements, identifying mispricings, and constructing trading strategies that exploit discrepancies between market-implied and actual reported fundamentals.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Multi-Domain Quantitative Factor Library
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset is a comprehensive library of quantitative factors designed for stock selection and risk modeling across global equities. It integrates hundreds of signals derived from regulatory filings, institutional ownership, sector-specific metrics, technical indicators, sentiment analysis, patent data, and alternative sources. The factors span multiple domains, including banking, technology, real estate, health care, and energy, and leverage both numerical and textual data using advanced techniques such as natural language processing and network analysis. By providing diverse, uncorrelated signals and sector-specific insights, the dataset enables investors and researchers to enhance alpha generation, improve risk management, and develop robust predictive models for price movements in various market environments.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: China Retail Investor Sentiment Analytics
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive analytics on retail and professional investor sentiment for Hong Kong and US stocks, derived from major Chinese financial social media platforms. It includes granular metrics such as the volume and sentiment (positive, neutral, negative) of posts, user engagement statistics (likes, replies, retweets, favourites), and sentiment indices for both registered and non-registered users. By aggregating and quantifying investor opinions and reactions, the dataset enables researchers and analysts to gauge market mood shifts, identify emerging trends, and anticipate potential price movements driven by retail and professional investor behavior. The sentiment scores and engagement metrics can be used as predictive factors in quantitative models, offering valuable insights for short-term trading strategies and risk management.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Securities Lending Insight Data
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBID) for global securities. It enables seamless integration and reconciliation of security data across different financial platforms and data sources. By facilitating accurate cross-referencing, the dataset supports portfolio management, trade processing, and data aggregation tasks. While not directly predictive of price movements, it is essential for ensuring data integrity and consistency when combining datasets for quantitative research, risk analysis, and multi-source analytics.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: VEI risk model
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides point-in-time, globally standardized fundamental financial data for over 47,000 active and 15,000 inactive companies across more than 100 countries. It offers daily snapshots of company financials, including original and restated values, with precise time-stamping to eliminate forward-looking and survivorship bias. The data includes annual and interim statements, business and geographic segments, ratios, and price/volume analytics, with history dating back to 1989 for US companies and 1997 for non-US. By maintaining a complete record of all changes and delistings, this dataset enables robust backtesting and model development, ensuring that only information available at each historical point is used. Its global consistency and depth make it highly valuable for predicting price movements based on fundamental factors, supporting both cross-sectional and time-series analysis.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Forecast Data
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset delivers full order book and top of book tick-level statistics for global markets, including bid and ask levels, sizes, order updates, trade prices, volumes, and interval-based metrics. It aggregates and computes advanced measures such as average distances from mid, size distributions, and volatility at various intervals. By analyzing these detailed order book dynamics and trade flows, users can detect liquidity imbalances, order flow trends, and microstructure effects, which are instrumental in forecasting short-term price movements and understanding market behavior at a granular level.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Multi-Factor Model
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive global equity ownership data, tracking holdings by institutions, mutual funds, insiders, and stakeholders. It aggregates information from regulatory filings such as SEC Form 13F, UK share registers, and other international sources, offering detailed position-level data including shares held, percentage ownership, and changes over time. The dataset enables analysis of institutional trading patterns, herding behavior, and the impact of ownership changes on stock returns. By monitoring shifts in institutional ownership and identifying high-conviction positions, researchers can gain insights into market sentiment, potential price movements, and the effectiveness of copycat or contrarian investment strategies. This data is valuable for constructing factors related to institutional activity, assessing market trends, and predicting future price movements based on changes in ownership structure.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Rapid Search Interest Signals
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset captures real-time search interest data for specific companies and regions, using a standardized algorithm to transform hourly search trends into a continuous, unbounded metric. By estimating daily search activity from high-frequency data and providing a confidence score for each estimate, it enables timely detection of shifts in public attention or sentiment. Such rapid changes in search volume can serve as early indicators of market-moving events, news, or shifts in investor sentiment, making the dataset valuable for predicting short-term price movements and generating alpha signals.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: AI Sentiment Score Data
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive analytics on news items related to equities, including over 80 fields across five key categories: relevance, sentiment, novelty, volume, and headline classification. Each news item is processed to generate asset-specific scores, such as sentiment (positive, neutral, negative), relevance to the asset, and measures of news novelty and volume over various time windows. The dataset also includes metadata like headline tags, company identifiers, and timestamps. By quantifying the tone, frequency, and uniqueness of news coverage for each company, this dataset enables researchers and quantitative investors to systematically incorporate real-time and historical news sentiment into trading strategies. It is particularly useful for predicting short-term price movements, identifying momentum or reversal signals, and enhancing alpha models with alternative data reflecting market perception and information flow.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: News Sentiment Scores
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides comprehensive, real-time financial news coverage for North American markets, including equities, commodities, forex, fixed income, and ETFs. It features detailed tagging by ticker, sector, region, and event type, enabling granular analysis of market-moving events such as earnings announcements, analyst rating changes, insider transactions, M&A activity, and regulatory actions. The dataset includes both firm-specific and marketwide news, with coverage extending to pre-market, regular, and after-hours sessions. By offering timely and structured news data, it allows researchers and traders to identify catalysts, monitor sentiment shifts, and backtest the impact of news events on asset prices, making it a valuable resource for predicting short-term price movements and developing event-driven trading strategies.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Website Popularity Ranking Dataset
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive ranking of internet domains based on passive DNS traffic, capturing the relative activity of websites across a global network. Unlike traditional site ranking models that focus on browser-based traffic, this dataset measures the number of unique client IPs interacting with each domain, offering a protocol-agnostic view of internet engagement. Aggregated metrics such as top percentile rankings, skewness, and kurtosis help identify domains with unusual or concentrated activity. By tracking changes in domain activity and popularity, analysts can detect emerging trends, shifts in user behavior, and potential catalysts that may influence the price movements of companies associated with these domains.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Short Interest Model
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset provides a comprehensive ranking of US-listed equities based on short interest metrics, intelligently normalized for market capitalization and adjusted for arbitrage strategies such as merger and dividend activity. It combines short interest data with institutional ownership, corporate actions, and fundamental information to generate percentile ranks at country, sector, and market cap levels. The dataset also includes a short squeeze indicator, volatility ranks, and other related fields. By identifying stocks with unusually high or low short interest and the likelihood of a short squeeze, the dataset is valuable for predicting potential price movements, especially in market-neutral, long/short, or directional trading strategies.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Sentiment Data for Equity
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset aggregates and analyzes social media posts and news articles related to financial markets, covering thousands of sources and several years of historical data. It quantifies market sentiment and buzz for individual assets, sectors, and indices using advanced natural language processing and machine learning techniques. The data includes sentiment scores, buzz indicators, and trading signals, which are statistically validated and can be used to identify shifts in market mood, anticipate volatility, and generate actionable buy/sell signals. By monitoring real-time and historical sentiment, traders and analysts can enhance their price movement predictions and improve portfolio performance through timely, data-driven decisions.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Deep Learning Stock Clusters
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset groups stocks into clusters using deep learning models that analyze 2D images generated from time series financial charts. By mimicking the perspective of retail traders, the dataset leverages convolutional neural networks to extract learned representations from price and fundamental chart images, then applies advanced clustering techniques such as k-means++ and dimension reduction. The resulting clusters reflect similarities in stock behavior, sector, and other financial characteristics, providing a high-dimensional, feature-rich grouping beyond traditional sector classifications. These clusters can be used to identify homogenous groups of stocks, improve portfolio diversification, and enhance risk modeling. By understanding how stocks are grouped based on complex chart patterns and features, analysts and quants can better predict price movements, uncover new sources of alpha, and construct more robust trading strategies.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Technical Indicator Chart Prediction
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset leverages technical indicator charts and image-based deep learning models to forecast future stock returns. By emulating the visual analysis approach of retail traders, it generates images from time series financial data—such as OHLC charts and various technical indicators—across different window sizes. These images are processed by pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to classify stocks into quantiles representing expected 10-day returns, with associated confidence scores. Covering the top 3000 US stocks, the dataset provides both raw and relative return predictions, making it a valuable tool for quantitative researchers and traders seeking to enhance price movement forecasts using advanced machine learning techniques and technical analysis signals.

GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.name: Deep Learning Technical Indicator Returns
GLB:1:TOPDIV3000.description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to analyze images of technical indicator charts, mimicking the decision-making process of retail traders. By converting time series financial data into 2D images, pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are used to predict future stock returns and their relative rankings across multiple time horizons. The dataset provides quantile-based return predictions, confidence scores, and cross-sectional rankings for a diversified universe of global equities. Its image-based approach captures complex market patterns and technical signals that may be missed by traditional time series analysis. This can be highly valuable for forecasting price movements, generating alpha signals, and constructing systematic trading strategies with improved prediction accuracy and low correlation to conventional models.
